 Judgment

This judgment is emerged consequent upon the petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of M.V. Act,
claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- on account of the death of Gopal.H. in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioners, in brief, is as follows:
On 12.03.2024 at about 1.00 to 1.05 p.m., the deceased was proceeding in the Bajaj Pulsar motorcycle bearing No.KA-51-J-6578 from Mattikere towards BEL Circle,
Gokul-Mattikere Main Road, Gokul bus stop side when he reached near M.S.Ramaiah home at that time, the BBMP Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-04-AB-9348 came from back side in a rash and negligent manner with excessive speed and dashed to the deceased's motorcycle.
Due to the impact, the deceased fell down on the road along with motorcycle and lorry tyre ran over the leg and hip of the deceased.
Due to which deceased sustained grievous injuries to leg and hip and other parts of the body.
Immediately, the deceased Gopal.H was shifted to Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru.
In-spite of best treatment given by the doctor, the deceased died on the same day due to accidental injuries.
Later dead body was shifted to M.S.Ramaiah Medical College and Hospital for postmortem.
After postmortem dead body was taken to their native place and conducted funeral and obsequies ceremony.
Petitioners have spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical and other expenses.
Prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy, working as porter and real-estate business and earning more than Rs.50,000/- per month and he was the only earning member in their family.
Due to the untimely death of deceased the petitioners have suffered mentally, physically and they have lost their bread earner.
The petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.2 is the son of the deceased Gopal.H., have lost their beloved care taker.
The respondents are the owner and insurer of the offending Lorry are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest.
3. In response to the summons, the Respondent No.2- insurance company appeared and filed written statement.
In spite of due service of summons, the respondent No.1 owner did not appear hence placed exparte.

Further contended that deceased himself is the tort-feasor and he was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-J-6578 without driving license and he was riding the same without observing the traffic on the high way on wrong side and caused the accident.
The driver of the Lorry was no way responsible for the alleged accident.
The driver of the BBMP Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-04-AB-9348 was not holding valid and effective DL and also the vehicle did not possess valid Permit and FC as on the date of accident.
It has denied the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased.
The compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence the respondent No.2 prays to dismiss the petition against it.

Whether the petitioners prove that, they are the legal representatives and dependents of the deceased Gopal.H.?

The petitioners to prove their claim have produced true copies of FIR, complaint, further statement of complainant, sketch, spot panchanama, Notice U/Sec.133 of IMV Act and reply to notice, MVA report, inquest panchanama, PM report and charge sheet which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 9.
10.
As per the documents, produced by the petitioners, Ex.P1- FIR is came to be registered on the basis of first information given by the petitioner No.1 Smt. Manjula.K.T.
On the date of alleged accident itself, the FIR was registered.
11. In the said Ex.P1, the first informant alleged the rash and negligent driving by the driver of BBMP Lorry bearing Registration No.KA-04-AB-9348.
In continuation of investigation, the IO conducted spot mahazar and rough sketch as per Ex.P2 & 3.
It is found that the accident spot is near to the cross road wherein the driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-04-AB-9348 dashed against the rear side of the motorcycle of the deceased.
As per the Ex.P5 IMV report the BBMP Lorry bearing Registration No.KA-04-AB-9348 has got damages in its front left side bumper.
The motorcycle of deceased has got severe damages.
It is alleged that the offending Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-04-AB-9348 came from Mattikere side and dashed against the rear side of the motorcycle of deceased.
This shows the gross negligence by the driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-04-AB-9348.

It is also established before this Tribunal that the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-04-AB-9348 was not maintaining safe distance and was driving his lorry in a rash and negligent manner and also was not in controllable speed as such, it dashed against the rear side of motorcycle of the deceased

. Thereby, the mahazar, rough sketch and IMV report marked at Ex.P2, 3 & 5 prima-facie establishes the negligence on the part of driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-04-AB-9348.
12.

Along with this if we perused the Ex.P6 inquest and Ex.P7 post mortem report it is evident that the death of deceased Sri. Gopal.H. was due to shock and haemorrhage as a result of multiple injuries sustained by him at the time of accident.

13. Further the Ex.P8 charge sheet is filed against the driver of the BBMP Lorry bearing Registration No.KA-04-AB- 9348 for the offences punishable U/Secs. 279 and 304(A) of IPC wherein the IO has opined that the negligence is on the part of the the driver of the BBMP Lorry bearing Registration No.KA-04-AB-9348.
No grounds are made out by the respondents to disbelieve the contents of charge sheet.

It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL)
319.

Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

In view of the ratio laid down in the authorities referred to above and applying the settled principle of law to the case on hand, which is further supported by the oral and documentary evidence adduced by PW-1, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident leading to this case indeed occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the BBMP Lorry bearing Registration No.KA- 04-AB-9348 resulting in the death of one Sri Gopal.H by sustaining injuries.
Wherefore Issue No.2 is answered in the Affirmative.
ISSUE NO.1 16.

As held herein above, the petitioners have proved that Gopal.H. died on 12.03.2024 due to the injuries sustained in RTA.

18. At the time of arguments the contention is raised by the respondent No.2 insurance company that the petitioner No.2, being the major son he is not entitled for compensation.

sentences.text:
"A claim petition filed by major married and earning sons of the deceased mother,
the Honourable Supreme Court held as follows:
"12.
The legal representatives of the deceased could move application for compensation by virtue of clause (c) of Section 166 (1).
The major married son who is also earning and not fully dependent on the deceased would be still covered by the expression "legal representative" of the deceased.

This Court in Manjuri Bera (supra)
had expounded that liability to pay compensation under the Act does not cease because of absence of dependency of the concerned legal representative.
Notably, the expression "legal representative" has not been defined in the Act.
"It is thus settled by now that the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to apply for compensation.

Having said that, it must necessarily follow that even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependant on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only.

The evidence on record in the present case would suggest that the claimants were working as agricultural labourers on contract basis and were earning meagre income between Rs.1,00,000/ and Rs.1,50,000/ per annum.
In that sense, they were largely dependant on the earning of their mother and in fact, were staying with her, who met with an accident at the young age of 48 years".

The judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.102868/2014 between Reliance General Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs. Gangappa and others held as follows:
"Having considered the principles laid down in the judgements referred to supra, this Court has taken note of recent judgement of the Apex Court in Birender, wherein it is held that even married sons are entitled for compensation not only on conventional heads but also on loss of dependency.

sentences.text: No doubt, both the claimants are grown up and self-dependent but that does not mean or can be construed that they did not suffer any loss on account of sudden loss of both of their parents.

It has been rightly contended by learned counsel for the respondents/claimants that son and the daughter with the death of their parents have lost protection, physical as well as psychological, besides sense of fulfillment of having parents to look after and cater to their daily requirements of life and emotional support.

No doubt, the parents were senior citizens but one has to take a realistic approach that they would certainly be looking after their grand-children for their nurturing, psychological and physical well-being, and would be a source of joy and happiness for the entire family.
By this loss the family has lost companionship, and the pain and agony that has accompanied this sudden loss can never be compensated in terms of money.
One cannot ignore the fact that Surinder Kaur even in her advance age would be contributing her lot in the household chores, cooking food, cleaning and such like daily duties.

The family claims to be having agricultural land besides having milching cattle and therefore, in rural household it is a matter of common knowledge that women contribute towards looking after the cattle and agricultural produce and contribute their lot towards the source of earning from these fields.

The learned Tribunal has lost sight of the fact in not awarding compensation on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses, which are handsomely part of calculations in such claim petitions.

Since there is no division of heads under which various amounts of compensation has been awarded, but having an overall look at the total compensation awarded in case of each of the deceased being ` 4.52 lacs and ` 3.50 lacs in lump sum and considering what has been left out as detailed in the foregoing lines, keeping in view the prevalent price index, there is no overwhelming occasion for this Court to show indulgence and thus this Court does not feel that the amount so awarded could be in any manner termed to be excessive necessitating intervention by this Court and rather appears to be just and appropriate in the prevalent scenario.
In the light of the same, the impugned award does not call for any interference and both the present appeals as such are disposed of as dismissed.

sentences.text: In this case, in the petition itself it is alleged that the deceased was doing real-estate business.
In the cause- title of the petition, it is shown that the petitioner No.2 is aged about 21 years.
The petitioner No.2 even though he is aged about 21 years, it is pleaded that he is the dependent.
No evidence is placed by showing that the petitioner No.2 is independently earning.
There is chances of children are still studying at the age of 21 years.
By applying the above precedents merely because the petitioner No.2 is major son of the deceased his claim cannot be rejected.
As such, he is certainly dependent on his father.
Accordingly, in this case the petitioner No.1 being the wife and petitioner No.2 being a major son is entitled for the compensation in accordance with their dependency.
Accordingly, issue No.2 answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE No.3:
23.

As held herein above, the petitioners proved that Gopal.H died on 12.03.2024 due to the injuries sustained in RTA, which is caused by the driver of the BBMP Lorry bearing Registration No.KA-04-AB-9348.
24.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be decided.
The petitioners have produced Aadhaar card of the deceased marked at Ex.P11.
As per the said document the date of birth of the deceased is 09.12.1975, the accident took place in the year-2024.
If it is considered, as on the date of the accident the age of the deceased was 49 years.
In the Exs.P6 & 7 inquest and postmortem also the age of the deceased was shown as 49 years.

Hence this court is accepting the age of the deceased as 49 years.
25.
As stated in the petition deceased was working as Porter and real-estate business and thereby earning Rs.50,000/- p.m.
To prove the said fact, the petitioners have not produced any document to prove the said fact.

In the absence of income, the notional income of deceased is considered as Rs.16,500/- p.m. as the accident is of the year 2024 and the annual income comes to Rs.1,98,000/- .
26.
As per Sarala varma case the proper multiplier applicable to the age of deceased is 13.

Since the deceased left his wife and son it is considered that, there are 2 dependents of deceased, hence 1/3rd is to be deducted towards his personal expenses, then the total loss of dependency would be Rs.17,16,000/- (Rs.16,500/- X 12 X 13= Rs.25,74,000/- minus 1/3rd (Rs.8,58,000/-) =
Rs.17,16,000/-).

27. In Civil Special leave petition (Civil No.25590/2014 dated 31.10.2016 (National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi & others), the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that "While determining the income, in case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.

30. The Petitioners are the wife and son of the deceased.
The wife petitioner No.1 lost her loving husband, companion and she has to the live remaining part of her life without him.
The petitioner No.2 is the son of the deceased and he lost his loving father.
Therefore they are entitled to a sum of Rs.48,000/- (Rs.40,000/x 10% hike every three years from 2017 as per Pranay Sethi Case) under the head of loss of consortium.

Further, I inclined to award a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards loss of love and affection, Rs.16,500/- towards loss of estate and Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses (this amount is calculated as per Pranaya Sethi case with enhanced rate at 10% after three years).
Towards medical expenses: The petitioners have produced medical bills as per Ex.P12 for a sum of Rs.1,23,578/-.
By looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, the petitioners are entitled for the same and no grounds are made out to deny the reimbursement of the medical bills.

sentences.text: Liability:-
In the petition it is alleged that the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the BBMP Lorry bearing Registration No.KA-04- AB-9348.
The respondent No.2 in its written statement has admitted the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle.
Even though the respondent No.2 has taken contention that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid licence at the time of accident, no evidence is placed in this regard.
In the charge sheet also no offences are invoked against the driver of offending vehicle for driving the said vehicle without having licence.
Accordingly, the respondent No.2 insurance company shall indemnify the liability of respondent No.1 owner and they are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
The petitioners are entitled for the interest at 6% per annum.
Accordingly, this issue answered in the affirmative.
ISSUE NO.4- 33.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.21,42,178 /-
 (Rupees Twenty-one lakhs Forty Two  Thousand One hundred and Seventy-  Eight only).
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
The petitioners are entitled with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,. from the date of petition till the realization from respondents on the awarded amount.
The petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled for the compensation at the ratio of 60:40.
The respondent No.2 - insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.

Out of awarded amount of petitioner No.1 and 2, 50% shall be released to petitioner No.1 and 2, on their proper identification and remaining 50% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in their names in any Scheduled Bank, for a period of three years.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw the award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.issue:
5. On the basis of the rival contentions, the following issues were framed by this court:
ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioners prove that, they are the legal representatives and dependents of the deceased Gopal.H.?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased Gopal.H had died due to the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident that occurred on 12.03.2024 at about 1.00 to 1.05 p.m., near MS Ramaiah Home, Near BEL Circle, Gokul-Mattikere main road, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of driver of BBMP Lorry bearing Registration No.KA-04-AB-9348 as alleged?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as claimed?
If so, what amount and From whom?
4. What order or award?
opennyai_summary.arguments:
It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL)
319.
It has been rightly contended by learned counsel for the respondents/claimants that son and the daughter with the death of their parents have lost protection, physical as well as psychological, besides sense of fulfillment of having parents to look after and cater to their daily requirements of life and emotional support.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.
Act, 1988 (in short, 'the Act') admittedly is a welfare Manjula K T vs Lakshmanaraju M on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23633200/
6 statute for the betterment of the claimants.
No doubt, both the claimants are grown up and self-dependent but that does not mean or can be construed that they did not suffer any loss on account of sudden loss of both of their parents.
No doubt, the parents were senior citizens but one has to take a realistic approach that they would certainly be looking after their grand-children for their nurturing, psychological and physical well-being, and would be a source of joy and happiness for the entire family.
By this loss the family has lost companionship, and the pain and agony that has accompanied this sudden loss can never be compensated in terms of money.
One cannot ignore the fact that Surinder Kaur even in her advance age would be contributing her lot in the household chores, cooking food, cleaning and such like daily duties.
The family claims to be having agricultural land besides having milching cattle and therefore, in rural household it is a matter of common knowledge that women contribute towards looking after the cattle and agricultural produce and contribute their lot towards the source of earning from these fields.
The learned Tribunal has lost sight of the fact in not awarding compensation on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses, which are handsomely part of calculations in such claim petitions.
Since there is no division of heads under which various amounts of compensation has been awarded, but having an overall look at the total compensation awarded in case of each of the deceased being ` 4.52 lacs and ` 3.50 lacs in lump sum and considering what has been left out as detailed in the foregoing lines, keeping in view the prevalent price index, there is no overwhelming occasion for this Court to show indulgence and thus this Court does not feel that the amount so awarded could be in any manner termed to be excessive necessitating intervention by this Court and rather appears to be just and appropriate in the prevalent scenario.
19. On the same point of law in the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Kerala reported in 2021 SCC Online Kerala 3209 (United India Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Shalumol and Others).
In the cause- title of the petition, it is shown that the petitioner No.2 is aged about 21 years.
The petitioner No.2 even though he is aged about 21 years, it is pleaded that he is the dependent.
No evidence is placed by showing that the petitioner No.2 is independently earning.
There is chances of children are still studying at the age of 21 years.
By applying the above precedents merely because the petitioner No.2 is major son of the deceased his claim cannot be rejected.
As such, he is certainly dependent on his father.
Accordingly, in this case the petitioner No.1 being the wife and petitioner No.2 being a major son is entitled for the compensation in accordance with their dependency.
opennyai_summary.decision:
30. The Petitioners are the wife and son of the deceased.
Therefore they are entitled to a sum of Rs.48,000/- (Rs.40,000/x 10% hike every three years from 2017 as per Pranay Sethi Case) under the head of loss of consortium.
Further, I inclined to award a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards loss of love and affection, Rs.16,500/- towards loss of estate and Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses (this amount is calculated as per Pranaya Sethi case with enhanced rate at 10% after three years).
Towards medical expenses: The petitioners have produced medical bills as per Ex.P12 for a sum of Rs.1,23,578/-.
By looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, the petitioners are entitled for the same and no grounds are made out to deny the reimbursement of the medical bills.
31. The petitioners are entitled for compensation under the following heads:
1. Loss of dependency Rs. 17,16,000/-
2. Loss of future prospects Rs. 1,71,600/-
3. Loss of consortium Rs. 48,000/-
4.
Medical bills Rs. 1,23,578/-
5.
Towards loss of love and Rs. 50,000/-
affection Total Rs. 21,42,178/-
In the charge sheet also no offences are invoked against the driver of offending vehicle for driving the said vehicle without having licence.
Accordingly, the respondent No.2 insurance company shall indemnify the liability of respondent No.1 owner and they are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
The petitioners are entitled for the interest at 6% per annum.
Accordingly, this issue answered in the affirmative.
ISSUE NO.4- 33.
For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.21,42,178 /-
 (Rupees Twenty-one lakhs Forty Two  Thousand One hundred and Seventy-  Eight only).
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
The petitioners are entitled with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,. from the date of petition till the realization from respondents on the awarded amount.
The petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled for the compensation at the ratio of 60:40.
The respondent No.2 - insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Out of awarded amount of petitioner No.1 and 2, 50% shall be released to petitioner No.1 and 2, on their proper identification and remaining 50% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in their names in any Scheduled Bank, for a period of three years.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw the award accordingly.
